title: CNNs and RNNs: Quick Revision to Transformers
summary: Quick revision notes on convolutions, pooling, CNN architectures, RNNs, LSTM/GRU and why transformers replaced recurrence. Covers mental models, core mechanics, comparisons and common mistakes, ending with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Convolution Basics: Filters, Stride, Padding
points: Convolution slides a small learned filter (kernel) over the input; each output value is the dot product of the filter with the patch under it, so one filter detects one pattern anywhere
Weight sharing and local connectivity: the same filter weights are reused at every position, so parameters = k*k*C_in*C_out (+C_out biases), independent of image size
Output size = floor((N + 2P - K) / S) + 1; example: N=32, K=3, S=1, P=1 gives 32 ('same'); N=32, K=5, S=2, P=0 gives 14
Padding: 'valid' = no padding and the map shrinks; 'same' = pad so output size equals input size at stride 1 (P=(K-1)/2 for odd K); stride >1 downsamples

Comparison: a 1x1 conv mixes channels and changes depth without touching spatial size; a 3x3 conv sees a neighborhood; two stacked 3x3 convs have a 5x5 receptive field with fewer parameters (18C^2 vs 25C^2)

chapters.title: Pooling and Feature Maps
points: Max pooling takes the max in each window (typically 2x2, stride 2), keeping the strongest activation and halving height and width
Average pooling takes the window mean; global average pooling (GAP) collapses each channel to one number and replaces big fully connected heads
Pooling has no learnable parameters and acts per channel, so channel count is unchanged and it adds small translation invariance
Comparison: max pooling keeps sharp features (common in early or middle layers); average pooling smooths and is used at the end (GAP); a stride-2 conv is a learnable alternative to pooling
Mistake: pooling too early or too often throws away spatial detail needed for segmentation or detection; shape tracking is (N,C,H,W) in PyTorch vs (N,H,W,C) in TensorFlow

chapters.title: CNN Architectures
points: Standard CNN pipeline: [conv -> activation (ReLU) -> pool] repeated, with channels growing and spatial size shrinking, then flatten or GAP and a dense softmax classifier
LeNet and AlexNet: LeNet is the small early conv-pool-dense design; AlexNet went deeper with ReLU, dropout and GPU training
VGG stacks only 3x3 convs with 2x2 pooling, simple and deep but very heavy in parameters (large fully connected layers)
ResNet adds skip connections: output = F(x) + x, so layers learn a residual and gradients flow through the identity path, making 50-150+ layer nets trainable
Comparison: Inception uses parallel multi-size filters with 1x1 bottlenecks; MobileNet uses depthwise separable convs for cheap mobile models; EfficientNet scales depth, width and resolution together

chapters.title: RNNs, Vanishing Gradients, LSTM and GRU
points: RNN: h_t = tanh(W_h*h_{t-1} + W_x*x_t + b); the same weights are applied at every time step and the hidden state h carries memory of the sequence
Training uses backpropagation through time (BPTT); the gradient is a product of many Jacobians, so it vanishes (<1 factors, can't learn long-range dependencies) or explodes (>1 factors)
Fixes: gradient clipping for exploding gradients; gated cells (LSTM/GRU) and good initialization for vanishing gradients
LSTM has a cell state plus forget, input and output gates; the cell update c_t = f_t*c_{t-1} + i_t*g_t is additive, which keeps gradients alive over long spans

GRU merges cell and hidden state with just update and reset gates: fewer parameters and faster than LSTM, with similar accuracy on many tasks; mistake: forgetting batch_first and the (batch, time, features) shape, or padding without masking

chapters.title: Why Transformers Replaced RNNs
points: RNNs process tokens one at a time, so training cannot be parallelized across the sequence; transformers process all tokens at once, which maps well to GPUs
Self-attention connects any two positions in one step (path length O(1) vs O(n) in an RNN), so long-range dependencies do not fade through repeated state updates
Attention: softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V; positional encodings are required because attention itself has no notion of order
Trade-off: self-attention costs O(n^2) in sequence length for memory and compute, while an RNN is O(n) with constant-size state, so RNNs remain cheaper for very long streaming inference
Mistake: assuming CNNs and RNNs are obsolete; CNNs still dominate efficient vision and edge models, and state-space/linear-recurrent models revisit recurrence for long sequences

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: CNNs, RNNs, Transformers
points: Conv output size: floor((N+2P-K)/S)+1; params per conv layer: K*K*C_in*C_out + C_out
Pooling: max keeps strong features, GAP replaces dense heads, no learnable weights; stride-2 conv can replace it
Architecture picks: VGG simple/heavy, ResNet skip connections, Inception parallel filters, MobileNet depthwise separable for mobile
Sequence picks: RNN simple but vanishing gradients; LSTM 3 gates + cell state; GRU 2 gates, lighter; clip gradients for explosions
Transformer: parallel training and O(1) path length via attention, but O(n^2) cost; choose by data type (images -> CNN, text -> transformer) and sequence length
